items.name: actionlint (GitHub Actions checker)
items.summary: Static checker for GitHub Actions workflow files.
items.why: Catches mistakes in CI workflows (bad expressions, unknown inputs, shell errors) before they fail on GitHub.
permissions: Reads the workflow files it's given; makes no network calls
Runs shellcheck and pyflakes on run: scripts when they're on your PATH

reviews.notes: All 5 sha256 pins equal GitHub's digests and the upstream checksums file; SLSA provenance verified (gh attestation verify, darwin-x64) to release.yaml at v1.7.12 (914e7df). MIT. No network code in the binary. docs/catalog-reviews/2026-10-30.md

items.name: Security Audit (Cloudflare)
items.summary: Six-phase security audit that produces machine-readable findings.
items.why: Claude reviews your code like a security auditor and reports only problems it can back with evidence, each with steps to check it, instead of generic advice. A full audit is thorough, slow and uses many model calls, so run it on demand (for example before a release), not on every change.
permissions: In a full audit, spawns many subagents (4 to map the code, then hunters, reviewers and verifiers), which uses a lot of model usage
Writes its reports outside the project, by default in ~/security-audit-skill/<repo>/run-<N>
Runs the project's build and tests only inside an OS sandbox without network; without one it only reads code
Runs node to check its own report files (the validators use only the file system)
items.notes: Not approved yet (docs/catalog-reviews/2026-10-30.md). All 20 files at c1c8a8c were read (tree hash matches): no network calls or install steps, validators use only the file system. Its MIT notice lives at the repo root and is copied into the skill folder as LICENSE, pinned by its own sha256 (M2-29). On Windows the validators reject all input, so a full audit can't finish there; guidance mode works.

items.name: Code Review
items.summary: Reviews a pull request with several specialized agents and keeps only confident findings.
items.why: Before you merge, several review agents check a GitHub pull request for clear bugs and for breaks of your CLAUDE.md rules. Each finding is double-checked, so only issues they are sure about are reported.

requires.hint: Install the GitHub CLI (https://cli.github.com) and run gh auth login in your own terminal

permissions: Adds a /code-review command
When you run it: reads a GitHub pull request with gh and runs 7 or more review agents (Haiku, Sonnet and Opus) that count against your Claude plan
With --comment: posts the review on the pull request with your gh login, without asking each time

reviews.notes: Read plugin.json, commands/code-review.md, README and LICENSE at f8c5e7a (1.0.1): Apache-2.0; one command, no hooks, MCP servers, scripts or telemetry. Pre-approves read-only gh calls and gh pr comment; posts only with --comment; spawns review agents including Opus. docs/catalog-reviews/2026-10-30.md

items.name: Codebase memory (code graph MCP)
items.summary: A local knowledge graph of the codebase that Claude queries instead of reading files one by one.
items.why: Claude answers "who calls this?" or "what breaks if I change it?" from an index of the code, which is faster and uses far fewer tokens than searching file by file.
permissions: Indexes code into a local database in ~/.cache/codebase-memory-mcp, shared by every project and agent on this account

Starts a per-account background process that watches the git projects of open sessions and re-indexes them; it coordinates through a folder in /tmp (macOS, Linux) or %LOCALAPPDATA% (Windows), and an index it was asked to build keeps running after the request ends

Serves a web UI (CBM Lens) on 127.0.0.1:9749 by default, with no sign-in: any program on this machine can read the graph, browse folders, start an index or change its settings there. `codebase-memory-mcp --ui=false` turns it off for every agent on this account
Claude can ask it to index any folder on this machine, delete an index, or save design notes in the index

Runs git; the binary makes no network requests and collects no telemetry. The web UI's in-browser assistant downloads a model from Hugging Face only when you click Download (checked in the 0.12.1 source)
items.notes: AgentChainer never runs the project's install script: it edits the global config of every coding agent it finds and adds hooks, agents and skills. Only the binary is used, registered for this workspace. Re-pinned to 0.12.1, which has the security fixes 0.11.0 lacked (docs/catalog-reviews/2026-10-30.md); the draft review is in docs/catalog-reviews/2026-10-31-codebase-memory-mcp-0.12.1.md. As a community item it needs two signed reviews before it's offered. Its web UI is on by default and AgentChainer leaves that setting alone, because it is shared by every agent on the account. Every cbm process on the machine must run the same version, so another installed version conflicts.

items.name: Commit Commands
items.summary: Commands for committing, pushing and opening pull requests.
items.why: Turns the usual git routine into one command: Claude writes the commit message, pushes and can open the pull request.
permissions: Adds /commit, /commit-push-pr and /clean_gone commands
/commit stages and commits your changes; the git commands it needs run without asking
/commit-push-pr also pushes the branch to origin and opens a GitHub pull request with your gh login, without asking
/clean_gone deletes local branches whose remote branch is gone (git branch -D) and force-removes their worktrees, which can drop unpushed or uncommitted work

reviews.notes: Read the 3 commands, plugin.json, README and LICENSE at f8c5e7a (1.0.1): Apache-2.0; no hooks, MCP servers or telemetry. Pre-approves git add/commit/push and gh pr create; /clean_gone uses branch -D and worktree remove --force. docs/catalog-reviews/2026-10-30.md

items.notes: /commit-push-pr needs the GitHub CLI (gh), installed and signed in. The plugin doesn't scan for secrets; the gitleaks hook covers that.

items.name: Context7 docs (Upstash)
items.license: Apache-2.0 (plugin files); the hosted service is under Context7's terms
items.summary: Up-to-date, version-specific library documentation from Upstash's hosted Context7 service.
items.why: Claude looks up the current docs of the libraries you use instead of relying on what it remembers, which avoids outdated APIs.
permissions: Sends library names and your questions (written by Claude, may include project details) to Upstash's hosted service (mcp.context7.com)
May ask you to sign in to Context7

reviews.notes: Read all 3 plugin files at f8c5e7a: an HTTP MCP server at mcp.context7.com; nothing runs locally; no environment variables or secrets are read; any sign-in goes through Claude Code's MCP OAuth. docs/catalog-reviews/2026-10-30.md

items.notes: Hosted MCP only: the service can change without a new pin. At f8c5e7a the plugin no longer reads CONTEXT7_API_KEY (removed upstream in #6333), although its README still says so. The marketplace tags this entry community-managed; it's listed here as verified-vendor (author: Upstash).

items.name: GitHub (official MCP)
items.license: Apache-2.0 (plugin files); GitHub's hosted server (source MIT)
items.summary: GitHub's own MCP server: issues, pull requests, code search and the rest of the GitHub API.
items.why: Claude can read and update issues and pull requests directly, so tasks can start from an issue and end in a PR.
permissions: Acts on GitHub as you with your personal access token: reads and, if the token allows, creates or changes files, branches, repositories, issues and pull requests (including merging)
Sends your token and every request to GitHub's hosted MCP server (api.githubcopilot.com)

reviews.notes: Read both plugin files at f8c5e7a: a remote MCP server at api.githubcopilot.com with Authorization: Bearer ${GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN}; nothing runs locally; the server's default tool sets include write and merge tools. docs/catalog-reviews/2026-10-30.md

items.notes: The token is read from the environment by the CLI; AgentChainer never stores it (ADR-0002). Use a fine-grained token limited to the repositories you need. The plugin uses GitHub's full default tool set (read and write). If the variable isn't set, the server fails to connect.

items.name: Secret scan before each commit (gitleaks)
items.summary: Scans staged changes for API keys, tokens and passwords before every commit, on your machine.
items.why: Agents write and commit a lot of code quickly. A key pasted into a config file is caught before it reaches the repository, where removing it later means rewriting history and rotating the key.
permissions: Reads the staged changes of each commit, locally; nothing is sent anywhere
Stops a commit that contains a secret. Mark a false positive with a gitleaks:allow comment or .gitleaksignore; skip the check once with git commit --no-verify

reviews.notes: All 5 sha256 pins equal GitHub's digests and the upstream checksums file; no signatures or attestations (the maintainer builds the binaries), so the pin is the protection. MIT. Runs only git diff --staged; no network calls. docs/catalog-reviews/2026-10-30.md

items.notes: Teammates without gitleaks (or AgentChainer) aren't blocked: the committed hook prints a hint and lets the commit through.

items.name: Go language server (gopls)
items.summary: Gives Claude Go code intelligence and refactoring through gopls.
items.why: Claude can navigate Go packages and see compiler errors as it edits.

requires.hint: go install golang.org/x/tools/gopls@latest, then add $(go env GOPATH)/bin to your PATH

permissions: Starts gopls in the project

reviews.notes: Read the marketplace entry, README and LICENSE at f8c5e7a (1.0.0, the whole folder): Apache-2.0; a config-only LSP plugin that starts gopls from PATH; no hooks, MCP servers, scripts or telemetry. gopls may download the modules go.mod lists. docs/catalog-reviews/2026-10-30.md

items.name: Playwright browser (MCP, pinned)
items.summary: Microsoft's Playwright MCP server: Claude drives a real browser to check web UIs.
items.why: Claude can open your app in a browser, click through it and read what's on the page, so UI changes are checked the way a person would check them.
permissions: Starts your installed Google Chrome and visits the pages Claude chooses
Runs npx, which downloads the pinned @playwright/mcp and two Playwright packages from npm on first use
Has a tool that runs any JavaScript on your computer (browser_run_code_unsafe); Claude Code asks before each use unless you allow it
Starts each session with a fresh browser profile (--isolated): no cookies or logins are kept

reviews.notes: The 0.0.83 tarball's sha512 matches the pin and the registry, published with npm provenance. Read package.json, cli.js, index.js, README and LICENSE (Apache-2.0); dependencies are exact Playwright versions with no install scripts; no telemetry. Uses the system Chrome; browser_run_code_unsafe is on by default. docs/catalog-reviews/2026-10-30.md

items.notes: Pinned to an exact version, unlike the playwright plugin, which runs @playwright/mcp@latest. Claude Code asks before using servers from a project's .mcp.json. Needs Google Chrome (or run npx @playwright/mcp@0.0.83 install-browser chrome) and a display.

items.name: Playwright browser (Microsoft)
items.summary: Lets Claude drive a real browser: open pages, click, fill forms and take screenshots.
items.why: Claude can check a web UI end to end, the way a tester would, instead of only reading the code.
permissions: Starts your installed Google Chrome, which Claude controls; it can open any URL
Runs npx @playwright/mcp@latest on every start: whatever version is newest at that moment, not a reviewed one
Has a tool that runs any JavaScript on your computer (browser_run_code_unsafe)
Keeps the browser's cookies and logins between sessions
items.notes: Not approved (docs/catalog-reviews/2026-10-30.md): the plugin runs `npx @playwright/mcp@latest`, a floating tag, which ADR-0005 rules out. Use playwright-mcp, the same server pinned to a reviewed version.

items.name: Python language server (Pyright)
items.summary: Gives Claude Python type checking and code intelligence through Pyright.
items.why: Claude sees type errors and definitions in Python code like an editor does.

requires.hint: npm install -g pyright (or pipx install pyright)

permissions: Starts pyright-langserver in the project

reviews.notes: Read the marketplace entry, README and LICENSE at f8c5e7a (1.0.0, the whole folder): Apache-2.0; a config-only LSP plugin that starts pyright-langserver --stdio from PATH; no hooks, MCP servers, scripts or telemetry. docs/catalog-reviews/2026-10-30.md

items.name: Rust language server (rust-analyzer)
items.summary: Gives Claude Rust code intelligence through rust-analyzer.
items.why: Claude sees Rust type and borrow errors and definitions as it edits.
permissions: Starts rust-analyzer in the project; it runs cargo, which can build and run the project's build scripts and macros and download crates

reviews.notes: Read the marketplace entry, README and LICENSE at f8c5e7a (1.0.0, the whole folder): Apache-2.0; a config-only LSP plugin that starts rust-analyzer from PATH; no hooks, MCP servers, scripts or telemetry. The server runs cargo build scripts and proc macros, as any Rust editor does. docs/catalog-reviews/2026-10-30.md

items.name: Security Guidance
items.summary: Flags insecure patterns in Claude's edits and reviews the diff for vulnerabilities.
items.why: Catches injection, XSS, SSRF, hardcoded secrets and similar mistakes while Claude writes the code, not after it ships.

requires.hint: Python 3.10 or newer (macOS's built-in 3.9 runs only the pattern warnings)

permissions: Checks every file Claude edits for risky code patterns and warns Claude (local, no network)
After each turn, sends the changed code to Claude Opus for a security review that isn't shown in your session's cost (uses your Claude plan or API key)
After git commit or push, a background reviewer reads related project files and sends them to the model
Can wake Claude after it finishes so it fixes the findings
On first use, installs the latest claude-agent-sdk from PyPI (a few hundred MB, not pinned) into ~/.claude/security
Keeps a log and state in ~/.claude/security, which uninstall doesn't remove
Reports usage counts to Anthropic through Claude Code's hook metrics
items.notes: Not approved at f8c5e7a (docs/catalog-reviews/2026-10-30.md): its hooks pip-install an unpinned claude-agent-sdk at runtime, which ADR-0005 rules out, and its model reviews spend outside the session's visible cost. It's no longer in the baseline profile. If you use it anyway: ENABLE_CODE_SECURITY_REVIEW=0 turns off the model reviews and the SDK install; SECURITY_GUIDANCE_DISABLE=1 turns the plugin off.

items.name: TypeScript language server
items.summary: Gives Claude TypeScript/JavaScript code intelligence through typescript-language-server.
items.why: Claude can jump to definitions and see type errors like an editor does, instead of guessing from text search.
permissions: Starts typescript-language-server in the project

reviews.notes: Read the marketplace entry, README and LICENSE at f8c5e7a (1.0.0, the whole folder): Apache-2.0; a config-only LSP plugin that starts typescript-language-server --stdio from PATH; no hooks, MCP servers, scripts or telemetry. docs/catalog-reviews/2026-10-30.md
